item: ABC investigation: 27 approved data centres will escape the federal energy and water rules
grounds: Energy load or grid; Water use; Process / consultation / transparency; Climate or emissions
frame_summary: ABC analysis of planning records and company documents finds 27 approved-but-unbuilt data centres totalling at least 3.38 GW, against 162 existing facilities at a combined 1.5 GW as at March 2026. Because the proposed federal energy and water rules are not expected to be retrospective, this whole cohort escapes them. The Prime Minister is quoted: 'You can't retrofit. But as well, many of the centres which are under construction tend to be smaller ones.'

item: Hydro Tasmania to decide on Firmus request for 450 MW — about 30 per cent of state demand
grounds: Energy load or grid; Foreign ownership or sovereignty; Water use; Climate or emissions
frame_summary: Firmus Technologies has asked Hydro Tasmania for 450 MW across three sites - Launceston, Long Reach in the Bell Bay Advanced Manufacturing Zone, and Wesley Vale. That is roughly 30 per cent of Tasmania's current electricity consumption and would make Firmus the state's largest single user, ahead of Bell Bay Aluminium at 355 MW. A decision is expected by the end of 2026. Firmus has pledged to build 2 MW of new renewable generation for every 1 MW it uses, but says it will initially match with certificates - a pledge, not a status.

item: Goodman's Project Apollo approved after 541 days, with a single public objection
actor: NSW Department of Planning, Housing & Infrastructure
grounds: Process / consultation / transparency; Water use
frame_summary: SSD-74069708 determined on 2 September 2026: 135 MW, ~A$1.365bn, 4-10 Talavera Road Macquarie Park. The application ran 541 days and drew ONE public objection despite being exhibited as State Significant Development. The contrast with Goodman's own Project Mars - same operator, same corridor, 374 submissions - is the point: exhibition is necessary for contestation but plainly not sufficient. The approval specifies large-scale evaporative cooling, which consumes water, in the corridor where Project Mars disclosed 510,009 m3/yr of drinking water.

item: Bowen rejects claims of a carve-out after Queensland says it won the data centre energy fight
grounds: Energy load or grid; Climate or emissions; Process / consultation / transparency
frame_summary: Two contradictory accounts of the same national cabinet meeting. Queensland and the Northern Territory claimed they would not be forced to mandate renewables for data centres, and the Prime Minister appeared to give ground. Energy Minister Chris Bowen then rejected the idea of a carve-out: states may seek approval to use alternatives such as coal or gas, but the Commonwealth has the final say and the threshold will be 'very high'. Whether the national standard binds Queensland is therefore still unsettled.
representative_quote: States will be able to seek approval to use alternatives like coal or gas, but the Commonwealth will have the final say and the threshold will be very high.

In the Legislative Council (4 Mar & 13 May 2026) David Ettershank noted the plan "is referenced repeatedly on the government's website… yet it is not downloadable"; departmental contacts suggested it "has not been produced yet or is for internal government use only".
